verdict: Revise before the owner's questions go out. The design is not ready for implementation as written. Coverage is nearly complete: §3.1's six sources and their event types are either present or reported as differences (DASH periods, the player's lack of ABR, dropped frames in the offline decode, decode errors under Q09, HTTP status from log text). §3.2's API, its two subcommands, automatic detection, grouping by source with offsets, the example question and both acceptance tests are all designed, and §3.3 is planned under D-007 (Q36). D-068, D-069, D-002, D-007, D-046 and D-050 are respected; D-070's deferred interfaces are only named. What holds: every code claim the design rests on matches its cited file:line; the numbers trace to the runs, survey files or file:lines named, except those in the traceability issue below; design.md is byte-identical to its render from design/src and design/*.json (<out>/review-adversarial/runs/render-design.txt); it contains no local paths, names or emails; and the worktree is still clean at 75cf6e0. Five major problems. (1) The safeguard for Q02 (d), 'detectable from the report', raises false alarms on D-069's ad ladder: 75 of 200 frames are flagged in each pair (run axis-d-check), so the recommended time base loses its main argument. (2) The critical path contradicts the dependency table: the acceptance tests wait for WP05 and WP07 and their questions. (3) ctest runs each test case in its own process (run ctest-registration), so ladders are not 'made once per run' and the test-time accounting is wrong. (4) Several P-entries are design choices that change default outputs. (5) D-070's interfaces are not designed. Thirteen minor issues follow. Where Phase 3 stands: the surveys and the merged design are done, with one design run; nothing is implemented. Next: fix the issues below, then collect the owner's answers to the 42 questions. This review's evidence is in <out>/review-adversarial/ (runs/ and tools/), where <out> is the survey directory. Nothing outside <out> was written, and design.md was not modified.

issues.where: design.md §4.2 (the paragraph after the axes table), §1.2 K2, Q02 option (d) and its 'Why', R11, WP01 tests
issues.issue: The safeguard for Q02 (d) does not work as stated, and the recommendation rests on it. The design says (d)'s only failure (a varying frame rate, or missing reference frames) is detectable from the report alone, by comparing each frame's PTS with its position in its report sequence and flagging differences beyond half a frame. I applied the check as worded to testgen's reports. In reports/ad-x264.json and reports/ad-mpeg2.json (the D-069 ad shape, Q34 (a), the acceptance test proper) it flags 75 of 200 scored frames in each pair: reference frames 125-199, off by 3.000 s. It flags nothing in ad-x264-origin1.json or degraded-x264.json (<out>/review-adversarial/runs/axis-d-check.txt). Yet on that ladder (d)'s seconds are right: they equal playlist time (design-library run axis-ad; design-evaluation run 09). The cause is that a forward jump under 10 s stays inside one report sequence (src/VMAFAlign.h:114; testgen.md §3.5), and that is exactly how missing frames look. So the report alone cannot tell (d)'s failure from a legitimate timestamp jump at an EXT-X-DISCONTINUITY. A per-step version of the check fires at frame 125 too: the +3.04 s step in run 09. Every D-069 ad document would carry a false 'wrong seconds' warning, unless the check is dropped.
issues.suggestion: Say in Q02 that (d)'s failure is not detectable from the report alone. Specify the check against the reference's segment map: a PTS jump at a playlist EXT-X-DISCONTINUITY is expected, and elsewhere it flags missing frames. That needs the same input as (c). Alternatively, report 'PTS jumps within a report sequence' without claiming the seconds are wrong. Add a WP01 unit test on the D-069 ad shape that states the expected warning. Then let the owner compare (c) and (d) on that basis.

issues.where: design.md §14: the WP09 and WP11 rows, 'Order and the critical path' items 4-5, and the critical-path paragraph
issues.issue: The critical path contradicts the dependency table. WP09 depends on WP01 to WP08, which includes WP05 and WP07 (the table; item 4: 'WP09's integration once WP01 to WP08 have merged'). WP11 depends on WP09 and WP07, and keeps all three tests in one file, tests/test_attribution_acceptance.cpp. Yet the paragraph says the acceptance path is WP00 → {WP01, WP02, WP03, WP04, WP06, WP10} → WP08 → WP09 → WP11, that test 3 'adds WP07', and that WP05 'is on no acceptance test's path'. In fact the two §3.2 acceptance tests (the paper's E1) cannot run until the binary SCTE-35 decoder and the session/fetch package have merged. That also makes them wait for questions the D-069 ladders don't need: Q14-Q16, Q18 and Q21 through WP05, and Q03, Q07, Q10-Q12 and Q41 through WP07.
issues.suggestion: Make the integration work without the optional inputs. Either split WP09 into WP09a (ladder-only build and CLI, depending on WP01-WP04, WP06 and WP08) and WP09b (sessions and fetch, decoded messages, depending on WP05 and WP07), or let TimelineBuild accept empty session and message inputs through WP00's stubs. Split WP11 into the acceptance tests (after WP09a and WP10) and the composite test 3 (after WP09b). Then recompute the Blocked-by sets and the critical path.

issues.where: design.md §9.5, P-Q, P-U, R9; WP10 and WP11 ('each ladder made once per test run')
issues.issue: The ctest time model rests on a false premise. P-Q, §9.5 and R9 assume each synthetic ladder is made once per test run, 'as tests/test_vmaf_ladder.cpp:192-216 makes its fixtures', which gives four ladders per run under Q34 (d). That fixture is a function-local static, so it is built once per process. The repository registers its tests with catch_discover_tests (CMakeLists.txt:371). In the debug build, all 359 of the 359 add_test() calls run mirage_tests with a single test-case name, so every Catch2 test case is its own process (<out>/review-adversarial/runs/ctest-registration.txt). TestTemp's directory is also per process and is removed at exit (tests/TestTemp.h:3-7). Under ctest, then, each case regenerates its ladders: test 1, each timestamp variant of test 2, test 3 (the ad ladder again), and test_synthetic_ladder's own generations. One generation took 2.022 to 2.313 s optimized and 16.941 s unoptimized (testgen.md §3.4). With ctest -j, cases that keep their media under MIRAGE_KEEP_MEDIA=<dir> (P-U) write into one directory at the same time.
issues.suggestion: Generate the ladders once per ctest run with a CTest fixture: a setup test (FIXTURES_SETUP and FIXTURES_REQUIRED, wired by WP00) writes them to a build-tree directory keyed by the generator's version. Alternatively, put the cases in one TEST_CASE with SECTIONs. Count generations per ctest run, not per process, in §9.5 and R9, and give each case its own subdirectory under MIRAGE_KEEP_MEDIA.

issues.where: design.md:9 (Conventions), §13 P-G, P-H, P-K, P-AA, P-AB, P-AE, P-P; §1.2 K17
issues.issue: The owner questions are incomplete: some P-entries are design choices that change default outputs. design.md:9 says every design choice is an owner question and that P-entries are implementation details that don't need the owner; docs/DECISIONS.md:7 says the agent makes only measurement and process choices. Yet these P-entries decide what an attribution lists. P-G: one PTS mismatch drops a variant's whole segment map and every segment-bound event. P-H: where unpaired frames, the master request and playlist requests sit, and that segment requests sit on media spans rather than in wall time. P-K: an OATCLS or DATERANGE message in a CUE-OUT's segment makes one cue_out, not two. P-AA: which BANDWIDTH ranks a rung. P-AB: every rung's copy of a tag is kept and listed, so a pair's answer shows both the reference's and the distorted variant's copy. P-AE: where a drop's interval ends on a coarser grid. P-P: plans with gaps or overlaps, such as a later player log with seeks, are refused.
issues.suggestion: Move these into owner questions with their alternatives, for example a single 'event-model defaults' question with one item each. Or mark them in §13 as design choices that need the owner's decision, not only confirmation. Keep only true process choices (P-A, P-J, P-L, P-T, P-W, P-I's ordering algorithm and the like) as P-entries.

issues.where: design.md §5.4 (the 'period' type), §5.5 'Interfaces only', Q20, R19, Appendix B (CuePayload, scte35_events), WP04, WP05
issues.issue: D-070 leaves DASH's EventStream and SCTE-35 carried within MPEG-TS segments 'as interfaces' (docs/DECISIONS.md:703). The design names these interfaces but defines none: there is no type, function, header, work package or test, only a reserved and unused 'period' type. The one generic carrier is Appendix B's CuePayload {segment, line, form, bytes}, and both it and Q14's placement are anchored to a playlist segment and line. Neither deferred carriage has such an anchor: an EventStream event has a period-relative presentationTime, and an in-segment section has a packet PTS (or, in the one public VOD stream found, an ID3 PRIV frame at a PTS, scte35.md §8). A later reader could not plug in without changing the core's types.
issues.suggestion: Define the extension point now: a cue input of the form {carrier: playlist-tag | dash-eventstream | ts-section | id3-priv; anchor: playlist position | media PTS on the carrying variant | period time; bytes}. Add it to WP00's declarations and have Scte35Events place every kind of anchor. Give WP05 a unit test that feeds a PTS-anchored section. State that Phase 3 builds no reader for either carriage.

issues.issue: The recommended session-drop semantics (Q22 (c)) leave several cases open, and Q23 (a)'s trade-offs omit its blind start. Open cases: (i) Is a clipped piece shorter than N+1 points still a drop? The prototype keeps pieces of any length (detection_semantics.py:138-157). (ii) Do two variants' drops that touch at a switch merge into one session drop? (iii) Which baseline does a piece report: the pair's at its drop's first point, which may lie before the span (as the prototype does), or the baseline at the span's start? Q23 (a)'s warm-up of W/2 non-low points means the first W/2 points of every curve can never be found low, so a degraded first segment is missed; its trade-offs don't say so. Q22's claim that under (b) 'whether a switch is a drop flips with small changes of T' has no run in the design's records. This review's run supports it. For the switch-down plan: a drop at frames 164-182 at T = 5, no drop at T = 5.5 to 8, and a drop at 125-199 or 126-199 at T = 3 or 4 (<out>/review-adversarial/runs/switch-t-sweep.txt).
issues.suggestion: Specify the N rule after clipping, whether pieces merge at switches, and which baseline is reported. Add the blind start to Q23's trade-offs. Add a WP02 test for each case. Cite a run for the T-sensitivity claim.

issues.where: design.md §6.1 and Appendix B (attribute(), Curve, Timeline::curves); the 'Why' of Q28; the last paragraph of §6.4
issues.issue: The API cannot express a session's attribution. attribute(const Timeline&, const Curve&, Interval, const QueryOptions&) takes a Curve. A session's curve, though, is derived and not stored (§4.4), Curve carries one variant, and Timeline::curves holds only pairs. So Q28 (a)'s session scope (the played variant's events per span, the reference's events and the session's own) has no input in the signature. Separately, Q28's claim that design-evaluation run 10 'used it' holds for pairs only: run 10's session attribution lists v180's events and not the reference v360's. Under Q22 (c) with Q28 (a), §6.4's 'the same events are listed' is therefore not exact: v360's copies would be added.
issues.suggestion: Add an overload that takes a Session, or a CurveRef {pair k | session id} that carries the spans. Correct the statements in Q28 and §6.4, or rerun the prototype with Q28 (a)'s session scope.

issues.issue: Some claims go beyond their cited sources, and some citations are wrong. (a) 'Every T from 3 to 40 and N from 1 to 24' (§2, Q23 (a)): run 05 measured a grid, T ∈ {3,4,5,6,7,8,10,12,15,20,25,30,40} and N ∈ {1,2,3,4,5,8,12,16,20,24}, not every value. (b) 'The pinned parameters pass with both encoders' (K20, Q33 (c), R17): run 05's MPEG-2 curves are the degraded ladder and the ad from the main origin only. The ad from 1 s and the continuous ad were not run with MPEG-2, and the continuous ad was run with neither encoder. (c) 'No seek reaches the frames of an ad whose timestamps restart' is called measured, but the probe's ad restarts at PTS 0.040 (experiments/hls-seek-probe/run-output.txt), not at the main content's origin as D-069's ad does. (d) §2's 'low frames exactly 75 to 124': testgen.md §3.2 lists frame 0 as well. (e) 'SCTE 35 2023r1 Tables 5, 9 to 15, 17 to 20, 27, 28' (§5.5) doesn't match scte35.md §3, which cites Tables 5-17, 20-25 and 29, including Table 23, the segmentation types Q15 uses. (f) Duplicate keys are refused at tests/test_vmaf_report.cpp:104, not at :26. (g) tools/mirage_vmaf.cpp:155 sets the log level; the claim that the callback is never replaced holds only because no other av_log_set_callback exists.
issues.suggestion: State the measured grid. Limit the encoder and seek claims to the cases that were run, or run the missing ones. Correct the table list and the two file:line citations.

issues.issue: §11's list of differences from the work order is incomplete. (i) §3.1 lists dropped frames under Decoder, but the design files them as vmaf/unpaired_frame (K15, §5.9), so §3.2's grouping shows them in the vmaf group. The merge table decides this; neither Q04 (a) nor §11 names it. (ii) Only observed events get a wall clock (Q03), so most events have none. (iii) A ladder without a session has no network events at all, and that includes both acceptance tests. Q10 also drops the sources survey's option of recording what the scoring reads saw (a per-input SegmentWatch recorder, labelled scoring-paced; sources.md §11, choice 5 (a)). (iv) Under Q13 (a), the decoder events that D-068's limits expect for frames dropped at a switch don't exist in Phase 3, so §5.6's 'as D-068's limits say' misstates them.
issues.suggestion: Add these to §11 and to the option texts of Q04, Q10 and Q13. Offer the scoring-read recorder as a Q10 option, with its D-007 and D-068 caveat.

issues.where: design.md §5.1 (the row 'a decoded splice time'), Q14 (a), WP05
issues.issue: A splice time is placed against the wrong clock. It is on the clock of the stream whose playlist carried the message, but the design places it at 'the first reference frame of the tag's sequence whose PTS is at or after it', comparing it with the reference's PTS. That misplaces it whenever the tag is in a distorted variant whose PTS differ from the reference's, which is every variant in mezzanine mode (D-002's alternative). 'The tag's sequence' is also ambiguous, because the report's sequences are not the playlist's discontinuity sequences (testgen.md §3.6, item 5).
issues.suggestion: Place the splice time against the carrying variant's own frames (from the demux pass), then map it to the reference through the pairs. Define the sequence as the carrying playlist's discontinuity sequence of the tag's segment. Add a WP05 test where the two PTS origins differ.

issues.where: design.md §5.5, WP04 (the handoff to WP05), WP05, Appendix B scte35_events(), Q17
issues.issue: Two gaps between WP04 and WP05. (i) EXT-X-CUE-OUT-CONT's SCTE35= form (§5.5) and cue_out_cont's 'the message if any' have no route to the decoder. WP04 hands WP05 only OATCLS's base64 and DATERANGE's SCTE35-* hex, and no test decodes a CUE-OUT-CONT message. (ii) Q17's break pairing has two owners. WP04 pairs cue-out and cue-in into ad_break; WP05 applies Q17's durations, merges a message into a CUE-OUT's cue (P-K) and pairs message-only cues. Yet WP05 depends only on WP00, although scte35_events() takes WP04's PlaylistEvents and edits its cue_events.
issues.suggestion: Route every embedded message, CUE-OUT-CONT's included, through CuePayload. Give ad_break pairing and Q17 to one package (WP05, made dependent on WP04). Add the CUE-OUT-CONT message case to the tests.

issues.where: design.md §3.2 file table, P-C, WP00, WP06, WP08, WP09, WP12, WP13, WP17; the 'Blocks' column of §12
issues.issue: There are gaps in file ownership and in the blocking lists. (i) WP17's new src/SessionLog.{h,cpp} are not among §3.2's files that WP00 stubs, so WP17 would have to edit CMakeLists.txt, which only WP00 may do (P-C). (ii) WP12 makes 'copies of nice_step and axis_label', while WP13 'uses the moved helpers' (ui.md §2.5 moves them). (iii) Q09 (b) adds a decode pass to WP06 (WP06 says so), but Q09 blocks only WP16. (iv) WP09's CLI defaults come from Q15 (--cue-types), Q16 (--bad-crc) and Q29 (margins), yet those questions don't block WP09. (v) WP08 writes the answers to Q02 (axis.kind), Q12 (spans[].scored), Q22 (detection.curves) and Q25 (detection.context_first), yet those questions don't block WP08.
issues.suggestion: Add SessionLog to §3.2's table and WP00's stubs. Choose between copying and moving the two helpers. Add the missing questions to the Blocks and Blocked-by lists.

issues.where: design.md §5.7, P-N, Appendix B (Request, fetch_session), WP07; §7 dispatch
issues.issue: Some edge cases of the session fetch are not handled. (i) SessionFetch assumes one NetworkLogger row per fetched file. NetworkLogger starts a row at each http.c 'request:' line (sources.md §3.1), so a redirected fetch gives two or more rows (from reading the code; not run). (ii) The logger keeps at most kMaxRequests = 4000 rows and evicts the oldest (src/NetworkLogger.h:194, src/NetworkLogger.cpp:389), so a long session whose rows are copied only at the end can lose its first requests. (iii) The fetch has no retries (P-N), while scoring retries a segment up to kSegMaxRetry = 10 times (src/VMAFSegments.h:28). One transient failure then records a failed request for a segment that was scored. (iv) The subcommands are dispatched before tools/mirage_vmaf.cpp:155-156, so run_timeline() must set the log level and call avformat_network_init itself.
issues.suggestion: Define how several rows map to one fetch and how the duration is measured across a redirect. Drain rows after each file. State the retry rule's consequence, or make retries an option. Note the setup steps in WP09. Add a redirect case to WP07's tests, which needs a new HttpFileServer rule owned by WP07.

issues.where: design.md §3.6 and §3.2 ('Not changed by any package'); Q37 (b)/(c), Q40 (b), Q41 (a)
issues.issue: The lists of what stays unchanged are incomplete, and two code comments would go stale. §3.6's exceptions name Q08 (b), Q09 (a) and Q13 (b) only. But Q37 (b) changes the render loop's seek handling, Q37 (c) changes Demuxer, and Q40 (b) changes ManifestParser, which §3.2 lists as changed by no package. Compiling NetworkLogger into mirage_vmaf (Q41 (a)) contradicts CMakeLists.txt:229-232 ('not through the player's ManifestParser and its network logger') and src/VMAFNet.h:8-9 ('mirage_vmaf doesn't link the player's FfOpen and its network logger'), and no package owns updating either comment.
issues.suggestion: List every answer that would change those files. Assign the CMake comment to WP00 and the VMAFNet.h comment to some package, or report both as stale.

issues.where: design.md §7 (Defaults, Detection), Q26 (a), P-AD, §10 ('around the frame')
issues.issue: Some defaults that change outputs or usability are not in any question. Under Q26 (a), W and N have no default, and `timeline` always detects (§7). So `mirage_vmaf timeline --report R --out T` fails without --window and --min-points even when only events are wanted, and no option skips detection. The default of attribute's --format is not stated. Nor is the interval the panel queries 'around' a clicked frame that lies outside a detected drop.
issues.suggestion: Ask the owner about a --detect on|off option, or about running detection only when W and N are given. State the default --format. Make the panel's query interval an item of Q39.

issues.issue: (i) The panel's off-main-thread load, its hash checks of the document and the ladder report, and the snapshot handoff all sit in the player-only TimelinePanel. ctest never covers them; only the scripted QA run outside ctest does. (ii) AV_PKT_FLAG_CORRUPT doesn't fall at the splice. testgen.md §3.6 (item 2) found it on the next-to-last packet before each splice. So corrupt_packet events placed 'at the frame' sit before the boundary that caused them, and an attribution of the ad's drop can miss the flag nearest the ad's start.
issues.suggestion: Move the loader and its checks into an ImGui-free unit next to TimelineMatch and test it in mirage_tests. Specify how corrupt_packet events relate to the segment boundary, for example by also attaching them to that boundary's segment, and test it in WP06.

issues.where: design.md WP15; §11 and §12, which are to be copied into docs/PHASE3_DECISIONS_PENDING.md; §10, which becomes docs/plans/timeline-ui.md; Phase 3's PR
issues.issue: WP15 would commit verbatim quotations of the work order to the public repository: §6.4's composite sentence, Q02's 'keyed by media PTS' and 'one time base', Q03, Q22, Q29's 'overlapping it in time', and §11 items 1, 4, 8 and 12. D-013 keeps the work order out of the repository (docs/DECISIONS.md:172-180). D-060 accepted Phase 2's rendering 'in its own words, with no passage of the work order quoted' as within D-013 (docs/DECISIONS.md:617; docs/PHASE2_DECISIONS_PENDING.md:228-241).
issues.suggestion: Paraphrase the work order in the documents WP15 commits and in the PR, as Phase 2's documents do. Add the check to WP15's cross-reference test, or ask the owner whether short quotations are within D-013.

issues.where: design.md 'Where Phase 3 stands' (WP00 'needs no answer'), WP00, P-AG, Appendix B
issues.issue: WP00 is marked 'Blocked by: none' and said to need no answer, but its shared declarations encode the agent's recommended answers: where events sit and the MediaKey (Q02), Event::wallclock_us (Q03 (b)), the Source enum in §3.1's order and the event vocabulary (Q04, Q30), Variant::rank_from_top and rank_from_bottom (Q07 (d)), PlanSpan {entry, first_seq, last_seq} (Q11 (a)), and Span::scored (Q12 (a)). Building them before the answers presents the recommendations as made. Any other answer then becomes a cross-package change routed through the lead (P-AG, R15).
issues.suggestion: Either block WP00's declarations on Q02, Q03, Q04, Q07, Q11 and Q12, or limit WP00 for now to the CMake wiring and empty files, and add the declarations once the answers are in.
